matches.quote: Each claim... rests on one device... with no data from other contact pairs, other devices or thermal cycles... show forward and backward D sweeps at fixed ν = 1.02
the three (1+N) devices sit at different θ (1.29°, 1.16°, 1.39°), so angle dependence and device-to-device spread cannot be judged.
The C = 3 → C = 4 transition in (2+4) L (D4) is not shown to be a topological, gap-closing transition rather than a first-order switch... or a domain mixture.
the "incipient fractional Chern insulator" at ν = 7/3 are not established... never states the expected Hall conductance or Streda slope... give fitted Streda slopes with uncertainties and ρxx
Novelty relative to Refs. [39–41, 54, 55] is not stated... Ref. [54] reports twisted (2+4) graphene, the same system as D4; Ref. [55] the twisted (1+N) family.
Quantization precision is never stated, and ρxx does not clearly vanish... tabulate ρxy/(h/Ce²) and ρxx in ohms at B = 0 and base temperature, with uncertainties
show whether the B = 0 remanent sign is set by D or only by history... measure the coercive field versus ν and D... device-to-device spread cannot be judged
extract activation gaps of both states versus D from Extended Data Fig. 5 and show whether the gap closes at the boundary
show whether the B = 0 remanent sign is set by D or only by history... Otherwise the D switching should be described... with the mechanism stated as a hypothesis
The claimed distinction from [32]... holds for any hysteretic switch... should also note that switching by B is generic to any ferromagnet.
Calling a state a C = 4 QAH insulator requires ρxx ≪ ρxy... clarify the convention, mark Δ and its sign relative to D
Ref. [39] is from the same group, covers twisted rhombohedral graphene with high Chern numbers and is the source of D3... state which observations here are new.

notes: C9 is marked 'partly' because P4 and P12 ask to quantify Hall quantization accuracy and residual longitudinal resistivity across states and temperature, but do not ask for tensor inversion to the conductivity tensor (sigma_xy, sigma_xx). C7 is marked 'partly' because P4, P19 and P21 ask for quantitative QAH criteria, clarification of the D sign convention, and explicit Streda fitting procedures rather than basic definitions of nu and D (which already appear in Methods). C13 is 'not raised' because P5 asks for multiple contact pairs to test twist-angle homogeneity rather than as an edge-vs-bulk transport diagnostic.
